html:
The Matenadaran is the museum and research institute of ancient manuscripts in Yerevan, opened in its building on a hill at the head of Mashtots Avenue in 1959, and holding about 23,000 manuscripts.

Its core is the old library of Etchmiadzin, taken over by the state after the Soviet takeover. It holds Armenian texts in the Armenian alphabet of history, medicine, philosophy and law, illuminated gospels by masters such as Toros Roslin, and works in Greek, Arabic and Persian, some known only from Armenian translation. The largest book, a homily collection of 1202, weighs about 28 kilograms. A statue of Mesrop Mashtots stands before the building. Many manuscripts were carried by refugees from the genocide.
